newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh sentenced to death Oklahoma City bombing.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh sentenced to death Oklahoma City bombing.

text.p: Convicted Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh was formally sentenced to death on Thursday for the 1995 explosion that killed 168 people.

Before being sentenced by Judge Richard Matsch, McVeigh broke his courtroom silence by quoting late U.S. Supreme Court justice Louis Brandeis as saying: "Our government is the hope and omnipotent teacher for good or for ill, it teaches the whole people by its example."

McVeigh, 29, had not spoken, except to answer a few questions from Matsch, during his 11-week trial which ended in June with a jury finding him guilty of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, in the worst attack on civilians in U.S. history.
It was not immediately clear why McVeigh chose to quote the Brandeis, who often opposed the use of government power against individuals.
Judge Matsch said: "It is the judgement of this court that the defendant be sentenced to death on each of the counts of the indictment."

He added that McVeigh had written him about his legal represetation and indicated he would make the letter public. McVeigh, in a newspaper interview published this week, said he was unhappy with his chief lawyer and wanted to fire him.
